channel.title: The Picky Reader — New Releases
channel.description: New and notable theology releases, tracked weekly.

item.title: The Death of Religion? — Byron R. Johnson and Thomas S. Kidd
item.description: A sociologist and a historian read the data on the rise of the "nones" and come to a different conclusion than the headlines do. Kidd's historical eye keeps the argument from becoming a statistics dump.

item.title: Developing a Healthy Prayer Life — James W. Beeke & Joel R. Beeke
item.description: Thirty-one short, practical meditations on prayer as communion with God.

item.title: The Theology and Theologians of Scotland — James Walker
item.description: Originally delivered as a series of Cunningham Lectures at New College, Edinburgh, Walker covers topics dealt with at length by Scottish theologians, including predestination, the nature and extent of the…

item.title: Pastoring the Whole Person — Erin I. Smith
item.description: In Pastoring the Whole Person, professor and research psychologist Erin Smith draws on two decades of work to equip church leaders with tools from human psychology so they can better understand and serve people…

item.title: Spurgeon: The Man Beyond the Pulpit — Ray Rhodes
item.description: Biographer Ray Rhodes focuses less on the thunder of the metropolitan pulpit and more on Spurgeon at home, tracing his inner strength back to the simple, quiet pastures of rural England.

item.title: The Tearing of the Temple Curtain — Adam W. Jones & J. Daniel Hays
item.description: In this book, Adam W. Jones and J. Daniel Hays argue that God the Father tore the curtain of the temple as an act of mourning over his Son's death. This interpretation has been neglected, though it has ancient precedent. In Jewish and Greco-Roman cultures, tearing clothes was a common expression of grief, and early Christian interpreters often linked this custom to the tearing of the temple curtain.

item.title: The Book of Psalms — James M. Hamilton Jr.
item.description: This translation takes a different approach. Intentionally literal and transparent to the underlying Hebrew, James M. Hamilton Jr.'s rendering lets the structure of the original show through, allowing readers to encounter the psalms' language and form in ways most English translations don't permit. Rather than smoothing the Hebrew into fluent English verse, Hamilton holds back and lets the poetry speak on its own terms, preserving and displaying the features that define it.

item.title: Create in Me a Clean Heart — Matthew Boswell
item.description: Based on sermons from Matthew Boswell, this devotional shares biblical wisdom and practical insights from Psalm 51, teaching readers how to have a heart that is repentant, restored, renewed, and…

item.title: Awake, My Soul — Dan Kreider
item.description: 365 hymns from the Middle Ages to the twentieth century, each paired with a brief meditation.

item.title: God's Ambassadors — Chad Van Dixhoorn
item.description: How the Westminster Assembly sought to reform English preaching.

item.title: The Undivided Life — David Gibson
item.description: This exploration of the New Testament book of James helps readers identify double-mindedness in their own lives and understand God’s grace as he “pulls apart the divided heart to make it whole.”

item.title: Worship and Wisdom for Formation and Flourishing — Ryan J. Cook & Russell L. Meek
item.description: Walking faithfully with God cannot be separated from humans' deepest emotional and spiritual needs.

item.title: A Woman's Place Is in the Story: Seeing Women in the Biblical Narrative — Sandra L. Glahn
item.description: A close reading of the women of Scripture and their place in the biblical story.

item.title: Come, Thou Fount of Every Blessing — Jonathan Gibson
item.description: A thirty-one-day liturgy for daily worship built on the Psalter, with historic prayers, creeds, and catechisms set alongside. The companion to Be Thou My Vision, and the same quiet discipline: someone else's words to pray when your own run out.

item.title: Holy People, Holy Land — Michael Dauphinais
item.description: God shares his perfect love with his creatures in covenantal relationships. For such love to be realized, the people must love God fully and become a holy people, and experience the indwelling presence of God by…

item.title: From Word to Worship — Michael Niebauer
item.description: In From Word to Worship, Anglican pastor and theologian Michael Niebauer unlocks the lectionary's full potential as a vehicle for Christian formation.

item.title: Bound and Free — William Marsh
item.description: Bound and Free is not only a theology for the Christian life or another book on how to effectively live by faith.

item.title: Doctrine as Discipleship — Heath A. Thomas
item.description: Why sound doctrine is essential to following Christ, not opposed to it.

item.title: Happiness — Andrew Wilson
item.description: Andrew Wilson uniquely weaves biblical, theological, philosophical, psychological, and sociological methods to answer 6 major questions about human flourishing in our broken world.

item.title: On the Resurrection — Gary R. Habermas
item.description: In this final volume of his magnum opus, resurrection scholar Gary Habermas delves into the profound implications of Jesus' resurrection.

item.title: A Covenant Feast — J. Ryan Davidson
item.description: Recovering a richer, more biblical vision of the Lord's Supper as a true means of grace.

item.title: Apocrypha and the Septuagint — Bruce W. Longenecker, Marieke Dhont & James K. Aitken
item.description: A scholarly introduction to the Apocrypha and the Greek Old Testament. Releases 8/11.

item.title: Interpreting Biblical Metaphors — Erin Heim
item.description: Biblical metaphors can be complicated and confusing. It can be tempting to read them as universal and context-free, assume they map directly onto modern life, or treat them as interchangeable with contemporary…

item.title: An Introduction to the OT — John Goldingay
item.description: Goldingay displays a robust confidence in the truthfulness of Scripture combined with a refreshing trust in the reader's ability to grapple responsibly with the Old Testament.

item.title: James Revisited — Brandon Crowe
item.description: Despite its reputation as an outlier, James resonates with the whole canon of the Bible. This letter refracts the Old Testament through Jesus's teachings in order to urge believers to maturity in the Lord.

item.title: The Four Senses of Scripture — Patrick Schreiner
item.description: For nearly 1,700 years, the church read Scripture through four interwoven lenses, literal, allegorical, tropological, and anagogical, known as the quadriga.

item.title: Exegetical Fallacies — D. A. Carson & Andrew David Naselli
item.description: D. A. Carson and Andrew David Naselli teach interpreters to think critically and to develop sound reasons for the choices they make. To do this, interpreters must reject unsound reasons; so the authors identify common mistakes many Bible interpreters make and how to avoid them.

item.title: Jerusalem Calls — Tammy Priest
item.description: In Jerusalem Calls, Tammy Priest tells the remarkable story of how God drew her to himself, and opens up the three Old Testament pilgrimage feasts that shaped her Jewish childhood to reveal something she had…

item.title: Connected — Gary Edward Schnittjer
item.description: An accessible, hands-on introduction to biblical hermeneutics built around Scripture's interconnectedness.

item.title: All-Sufficient God — Martyn Lloyd Jones
item.description: These mighty sermons from Isaiah chapter 40 show that the God of the Bible is not only the great Creator and Judge but the Father of mercies and the God of all comfort who meets us at the point of our deepest need.
